name: Comanda (Catalan unilateral comanda; comanda ad usum maris)
tradition: Catalan (Crown of Aragon: Barcelona, Vic, Mallorca, Valencia)
period: 1230s-15c (Vic acts from 1230-1231; Barcelona and Mallorca 1240-1450; Consolat de Mar comanda chapters as compiled 14c-15c)
key_source: SCOPE: the comanda in which the investor (comanador) supplies all the capital and bears its loss to peril, and the commendatary (comandatari) trades it for a share of profit, commonly a quarter ('ad quartum lucri'); chiefly by sea, also by land. SPLIT 2026-10-07 by MS's decision FROM comanda_ad_societatem ON THE LOSS RULE, NOT ON TERRAIN: Martinez Gijon 1966, 386-388 and 404-405 and Garcia Sanz 1959 show loss-sharing comandas by sea and land alike, and unilateral comandas without travel (Vic 1230); Fynn-Paul 2017, 91 shows that the land-sea distinction was not a contemporary one. SOURCES: Llibre del Consolat de Mar, ed. Capmany/Font Rius 1965 (XWHD38V2), caps. 88, 209-216, 219-220, 254, 279 - the normative layer and the tradition's own statements (cap. 211: commendataries 'lose nothing'); Martinez Gijon 1966 (AHDE 36, 379-456; sections A-B read) and 1974 (HID 1, 263-274) - the doctrine, quoting 13c-14c acts; Hancock 2025 (Oxford DPhil) - 1,432 Barcelona and Mallorca contracts 1240-1350 for the risk clause (352 acts), the profit split and the general pledge; Garcia Sanz 1959 and 1963 (Ausa) - the Vic acts; Cuadrada & Lopez Perez 1991; Polonio 2014 for scale (over 3,000 AHPB maritime comandas 1349-1450). OUT OF SCOPE, AND CODED FROM NOWHERE IN THIS ROW: the comanda-DEPOSIT ('in pura comanda sive deposito', regulated as Roman deposit by the Furs de Valencia 1240 and the Costums de Tortosa 1272), in which the depositary answers even for mischance and which therefore reverses CF2; the comanda of persons (apprenticeship), of castles (feudal tenure), of land (sharecropping), of livestock ad parceriam, testamentary and office commendas (Garcia Sanz 1959, Ausa 3 no. 30, 284-293); the comanda-prestec (Villalonga 2009, not held); the comanda de nau, the ship given in comanda (Consolat caps. 217-218); the Templar and Hospitaller 'comanda' (commandery); and Martinez Gijon's comanda-deposit used to clothe a transport-and-insurance contract (1974, 270-273, Madurell & Garcia Sanz doc. 255). NON-INDEPENDENCE, DECLARED BEFORE ANY COMPARISON: (i) Hancock 2025 includes 136 contracts transcribed by Madurell, so Hancock and Madurell & Garcia Sanz 1973 are one witness on what they share; (ii) Martinez Gijon, Garcia Sanz and Sayous code from overlapping published acts (Vic, Barcelona cathedral), so their agreement is not corroboration; (iii) the drafting descends from the Italian commenda and the Consolat's rules have Italian and Marseillais parallels (Pardessus II, ch. XII n.), so any agreement with commenda or societas_maris is PARALLELISM, not convergence. NOT YET CONSULTABLE and the subject of a later recoding when digitised by MS: Madurell & Garcia Sanz 1973 (VPX7DFWD, the anchor edition), Garcia i Sanz & Madurell 1986 Societats mercantils (AWXXX4UW), Noguera de Guzman 1967, Sayous 1931 (EUC 16; the PDF on 54KLRXV3 is Sayous 1936 instead), Del Treppo 1972. Polonio Luque 2012 text volume needs OCR (broken font). Martinez Gijon 1964 and section C of 1966 not yet read. Coded 2026-10-07, open (not blind), by claude-opus-5-5; batch record in records/NOTES-comanda-coding-2026-10-07.md when applied. name: Comanda ad societatem (loss-sharing comanda; comanda sive societas)
tradition: Catalan (Crown of Aragon: Vic, Barcelona, Manresa)
key_source: SCOPE: comandas in which a diminution of the investor's capital is borne by investor and agent in the proportion in which they share profit - halves, or thirds - until his capital is restored; the acts call them 'comanda ad societatem', 'comanda sive societas' or 'societas'. Mostly local trade and craft (butchers, shoemakers, a skinner), also by sea (Vic 1230, 1231, 1239). SPLIT 2026-10-07 FROM comanda ON THE LOSS RULE (CF2), by MS's decision. SOURCES: Garcia Sanz 1959 (Ausa 3 no. 30), 288 and doc. 5 (1273), the typologist's statement that local comandas commonly halve profits and losses; Martinez Gijon 1966, 386-388, 395-399, 404-406, who reads the craft as the agents' contribution and the form as 'bilateral', 'not substantially different' from the maritime bilateral comanda, and reads the 1230-1231 'societates' as comandas because only the agent gives guarantees; Fynn-Paul 2017, 95 n. 31 (Manresa 1323, 'ad terciam partem lucri et amissionis'). THIN EVIDENCE, DECLARED: about six quoted acts, mostly 13c, through two secondary authors who share an upstream (Carreras y Candi, Sayous, Garcia Sanz's editions); Martinez Gijon calls bilateral documents 'escasos' (386). Fynn-Paul's 91 Manresa commendas were not tallied for the loss clause. RELATION TO societas_maris: the Catalan counterpart of the bilateral commenda on the loss rule, but the agent's money contribution is a minority here (CF1=1 against societas_maris CF1=P); parallelism, not convergence.
